approachQuestion.prompt:
Voucher coverage

A sorted array values lists positive voucher denominations, one voucher per entry. A payment may use any subset of vouchers, each at most once. You may add vouchers of any positive integer denomination. Return the minimum number to add so every integer payment from 1 through target can be formed.

Example 1: values=[1,5], target=8 → 2. Add 2 and 4 to cover every amount through 12. One added voucher cannot fill both the gap at 2 and all amounts through 8.
Example 2: values=[], target=7 → 3, using 1,2,4.

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ min(200000,target); 1 ≤ values[i] ≤ 10^9; 1 ≤ target ≤ 10^9; values is nondecreasing. Input is read-only. Return only the stated scalar result. All arithmetic and comparisons use constant-time exact 64-bit operations; all intermediate values fit.

options.text: Maintain reach=0, meaning every amount through reach is formable. Until reach ≥ target, consume the next voucher v if v ≤ reach+1 and add v to reach; otherwise add a new voucher reach+1 and extend reach by that value.
options.feedback: If v ≤ reach+1, the old and shifted coverage intervals touch. At a gap, any added voucher larger than reach+1 cannot form that missing amount; choosing exactly reach+1 extends coverage as far as any legal gap-filling choice.

options.text: Add a voucher equal to the largest uncovered amount at each step.
options.feedback: The missing small amount remains impossible. With values=[] and target=2, adding only 2 still cannot form 1.

options.text: Return the number of integers in 1..target absent from values.
options.feedback: Subset sums, rather than individual denominations, provide coverage. For values=[1,2] and target=3 no addition is needed even though denomination 3 is absent.

options.text: Enumerate every legal sequence of decisions, evaluate each complete candidate, and return the best result.
options.feedback: Exhaustive search can find the right result, but revisits combinations of decisions that the safe local rule resolves directly. The number of candidates grows far beyond what the input limit permits.

If all amounts through reach are formable, a voucher at most reach+1 extends contiguous coverage. A larger voucher leaves reach+1 missing, so patch exactly that first gap; it maximizes new coverage without leaving a hole.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed frontier method. Let n be the voucher count and T=target. Use a single forward index and scalar reach and count, stop immediately when reach ≥ T, and use exact constant-time arithmetic. No input copy, subset table or recursion is used. Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound in the two independent parameters n and T (T ≥ 2).
constraints: Input and returned scalar are excluded. All other live storage, including copying and any call stack, is counted. No hashing or expected-time operations are used.

options.text: Time O(n + log T), auxiliary space O(1)
Time O(n + T), auxiliary space O(1)
Time O(n + log T), auxiliary space O(n)

feedback.reason: Consume each voucher once; each patch roughly doubles the covered range.

messages.text: Coverage expands by doubling on a patch; it is not processed amount by amount.
No per-voucher or per-payment table is allocated.
An empty voucher array can still require logarithmically many additions.

details: Each consumed voucher advances the index once. Every added voucher changes reach to 2*reach+1, so at most O(log T) patches are needed. Instances can require a linear input scan or logarithmically many patches, giving the tight combined worst-case bound O(n + log T). Only scalar state is stored.
n and T are independent; scalar iterative frontier; no copying, recursion or hashing.
